To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AMPA receptors are involved in nociception in the dorsal horn, while NMDA receptors and AMPA receptors are both involved in motor neuron function.
the expression pattern in the dorsal horn is very different from that of motor neurons.

the expression pattern and intensity of glutamergic receptors in the dorsal horn neurons differ from those of spinal motor neurons, and that the glutamergic receptors regulating motor neurons are different from those regulating sensory neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of glutamate receptors in nociceptive primary sensory neurons and spinal motor neurons, and with their functional roles in the transmission of nociceptive information.
the expression of the subunit of ionotropic glutamergic receptors in spinal sensory neurons, which are involved in the transmission of pain information.
the expression pattern of glutamergic receptors in the spinal cord, with special reference to the sensory and motor neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the AMPA-type and NMDAR receptors are differentially distributed and regulated in the dorsal horn, and that these differences are closely related to their roles in nociceptive and motor systems, and to their subunit compositions.
the AMPA-type and KA-type receptors are mainly involved in the transmission of nociceptive primary inputs, and that the NMDA receptor plays a more important role in motor neurons.
AMPA-type receptors, especially GluR2, are involved in the transmission of nociceptive primary sensory afferent information, while NMDA receptors are involved in the motor neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glutamergic sensory afferents are regulated by the glutamergic system in which GluRs 1, 2 and 4 play an important role in the superficial dorsal horn.
the AMPA-type, KA-type, and NMDA receptor systems are involved in the regulation of the spinal sensory neurons.

the expression pattern for the subunits of AMPA-type receptor in the spinal sensory neuron is different from that for the spinal motor neurons, and that the AMPA-type and NMDAs receptors in the spinal motor neurons are involved in different mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AMPA receptors, especially GluR2, are highly expressed in the spinal nociceptive sensory neurons, while the NMDA receptors, especially NR1, are highly expressed on motor neurons.

the subunits of AMPA-type and KA-type receptors are expressed in the spinal cord in a region-specific manner and that there are differences in the subunit composition between motor neurons and sensory neurons.

there are at most two types of glutamergic system which regulate motor neurons, and that the subunits of AMPA-type receptors expressed in the spinal motor neurons are different from those expressed in the spinal sensory neuron.
